objective: Make System achievement proposals deterministic and evidence-based from the immutable ledger while preserving the existing achievement write gate, quest/progression semantics, player-state permission boundary and all unrelated controller behavior.

roles_before.artifact: achievement.unlock already exists as an explicit System action validated through the shared action gate and requires verified evidence.
A real achievement unlock is a player-state mutation and requires separate exact permission under the System controller mutation rules.
Quest v2 completion and progression awards remain the canonical System-era evidence for rewarded execution; achievements must not create XP or coins independently.
Legacy Quest v1, infrastructure probes and pre-System life history are not retroactive System progression and must not silently become achievement evidence.
System Controller continues to own STATUS, quest, shop, skill, stat, achievement, log and explanation intents without changing their existing mutation boundaries.
The append-only system_events ledger is the one mutable owner of derived System state and is sufficient to reconstruct qualifying event linkage.
Base SHA 479a6c2afdf97c4826a99457b82fd281d89710a4 preserves the prior controller behavior where achievement eligibility had no deterministic policy.

role_dispositions.destination: No achievement action schema, PostgreSQL gate or event validation is changed; the new evaluator produces a candidate payload only.
Controller guidance explicitly requires presenting the exact achievement.unlock payload and evidence ref before requesting exact mutation permission.
Eligibility requires a verified Quest v2 completion linked as the basis of a verified progression.awarded event; achievements themselves issue no XP or coins.
system-achievement-ledger:v1 codifies the boundary: reported, legacy, unrewarded, expired/failed/cancelled and pre-System evidence cannot qualify.
The controller receives one additive Achievement Policy section; all existing intents and quest/shop procedures remain intact.
The pure evaluator reconstructs qualifying completion→Quest v2→progression linkage and emits a deterministic SHA-256 evidence reference from stable completion event IDs.
The exact base SHA remains a complete rollback point; the implementation is additive and introduces no migration or production data write.

capability_probes.assertion: Existing achievement.unlock model/PostgreSQL validation and projection behavior remain unchanged and pass the normal System regression suite.
Legacy Quest v1, reported completion, unrewarded completion and pre-System evidence cannot produce an achievement candidate.
Eligibility evaluation produces only an exact permission-gated action plan and never appends an achievement event or progression reward.
Quest v2, atomic resolution, shop policy, profile/calibration, deadline, session and retired-LifeUp regressions continue to pass.
Base SHA 479a6c2afdf97c4826a99457b82fd281d89710a4 retains the exact pre-policy controller and runtime behavior.

tests.expected: Only verified rewarded Quest v2 completions qualify; 1/5/20x28 milestones, unlock suppression, deterministic ordering/evidence and fail-closed inputs pass.
PASS with no production player-state or schema mutation.

verification.implementation_scope: Five intended paths only: architecture manifest, additive achievement policy/spec, pure ledger evaluator, focused tests and controller routing guidance. No migration, action-gate change, production data write or automatic unlock.
verification.candidate_ci_detail: Implementation head passed model tests, Docker smoke, real PostgreSQL action-gate plus HTTP-through-Postgres, and retired-LifeUp regression. The manifest candidate commit then passed architecture guard self-test, continuity coverage, System routing, Skill/Social and XMind regressions.
